page.layout: One page of text, with two round portraits at the top (medallions), then two paragraphs of text in a single column, then a heading "APPENDIX" at the right, then a decorative woodcut ornament at the foot. Running head at the top; page number at the top left. No margin notes.

main_text.p: [Portrait medallions: left "IO. GORREVS D. M.D."; right "LAVR. IOVBERTVS." — printed as legends on the medallions]

IOANNES Gorreus Parisiensis, Doctor Medicus, Latine scripsit Definitionum Medicarum libros x x iiii. literis Græcis distinctos, & iuxta Alphabeti ordinem. Ex Græco etiam Hipocratis Iusiurandum, De arte, De antiqua medicina, De medico, Latina ciuitate donauit. Vitam cum morte commutauit non multo postquam Christianiss. Henricus iii. Regni Franciæ suscepit gubernacula. Quantæ doctrinæ erat testantur nonnulli uersus Iacobi Greuini eius discipuli in limine Poematum Theriacōn, & Alexipharmacōn Nicandri Poëtæ Græci ab eodem Greuino è Græco uersibus Gallicis expressorum & eidem Gorreo dicatorum.

LAVRENTIVS Ioubertus, Valentinus Delphinas, Medicus Regius, post obitum Gulielmi Rondeletij professoris Regij & Cancellarij in schola Monspeliensi, in huius locum suffectus est, tanquam omnium qui tunc ibi degebant dignissimus: quod munus exercet hoc tempore: nec minus celebratur eius experientia in re medica, quam doctæ & exquisitæ illius Lucubrationes quas edidit tam in Latina quam vernacula lingua. Has videre licebit in Bibliotheca Gallica.
main_text.head: APPENDIX

page.notes:
The two medallion portraits are illustrations; their legends are transcribed inside the first

as bracketed description only. The woodcut ornament at the foot is decorative and not transcribed. Doubtful: "Greuino" and "Gorreo" are read as printed; "Monspeliensi" is printed with a long s in the original and is copied as printed, so the long s here is a transcription fault to check against the scan, as the rules require plain s.
